segment: large-print bold-line colouring for low-vision and limited-dexterity adults

observations: the bold-and-easy style is repeatedly described as growing faster than the titles serving it
buyers named are seniors, beginners, and people who find intricate adult designs overwhelming
forty designs printed single-sided is the common shape, giving about eighty interior pages
high contrast and thick outlines are described as the functional requirement, not a style preference
arthritis, tremor and reduced hand strength are named as distinct buyer needs alongside low vision
memory care and assisted living are named as institutional buying contexts
large open areas matter as much as line weight: small regions are unusable with a shaky hand

signals.segment: colouring buyer complaints across the category
observations: printing on both sides, causing marker bleed-through, is the most consistently repeated complaint
lines that do not meet, so fills leak across the page, is the second repeated complaint
inconsistency between pages within one book is a third recurring theme
some publishers print a note on reverse pages explaining the blank is deliberate

signals.segment: pricing observed in the bold-and-easy band
observations: the observed asking range for bold-and-easy senior titles runs roughly nine to thirteen dollars
the wider colouring category clusters lower, around eight to ten dollars

opportunity: The two most repeated complaints in this category, bleed-through and lines that do not close, are both mechanically verifiable rather than matters of taste. A book that can demonstrate it has neither, aimed at low-vision and limited-dexterity colourists, competes on the exact axis buyers complain about.
